venues.name: Emirates Palace Mandarin Oriental
venues.note: The capital's palace, gold-domed, ceremonial, and now in the surest of hands.

venues.name: The St. Regis Saadiyat Island Resort
venues.note: A long, protected beach and butler service, the calm cultural island, done grandly.

venues.name: Four Seasons Hotel Abu Dhabi at Al Maryah Island
venues.note: The surest hands in the city, service you never have to think about.
credentials: World Travel Awards, Abu Dhabi's Leading Luxury Hotel 2024

venues.name: The St. Regis Abu Dhabi
venues.note: A sky-bridge suite slung between two towers, with its own beach club below.

venues.name: Conrad Abu Dhabi Etihad Towers
venues.note: A landmark tower address on the Corniche, polished and quietly capable.

venues.name: Rosewood Abu Dhabi
venues.note: A glass tower on the financial island, run with Rosewood's understated grace.
credentials: Condé Nast Traveler Readers' Choice 2024, No. 6 Hotel in the Middle East

venues.name: Jumeirah at Saadiyat Island Resort
venues.note: Sleek, low and sustainable, opening straight onto a protected white beach.
credentials: World Travel Awards, Abu Dhabi's Leading Luxury Resort 2024

venues.name: Park Hyatt Abu Dhabi Hotel and Villas
venues.note: A low-rise beach house with room to breathe, the quiet Saadiyat choice.
credentials: World Travel Awards, Abu Dhabi's Leading Resort 2024

venues.name: The Ritz-Carlton Abu Dhabi, Grand Canal
venues.area: Grand Canal / near Sheikh Zayed Grand Mosque
venues.note: A Venetian-styled canal palace facing the great white mosque.

venues.name: The Abu Dhabi EDITION
venues.note: Ian Schrager cool on the marina, the city's most design-literate address.

venues.name: Fairmont Bab Al Bahr
venues.note: Framed views straight across the water to the Sheikh Zayed Grand Mosque.

venues.name: Shangri-La Qaryat Al Beri, Abu Dhabi
venues.note: A souk, waterways and abras, a resort village beside the Grand Canal.

venues.name: Zaya Nurai Island
venues.note: A private island of villas, reached only by boat, the quietest luxury near the capital.
credentials: World Travel Awards, World's Leading Luxury Villa Resort (multiple years)
Condé Nast Traveler, Most Incredible Private Islands

venues.name: Al Wathba, a Luxury Collection Desert Resort & Spa
venues.note: A closer, gentler desert escape, dunes and a serious spa within easy reach of the city.

venues.name: Saadiyat Rotana Resort & Villas
venues.note: A dependable beach resort on the cultural island, generous with space.

venues.name: Erth
venues.note: Modern Emirati cooking beside the city's oldest fort, a taste of the real capital.

venues.name: Hakkasan Abu Dhabi
venues.note: The Cantonese standard-bearer, holding its star inside the palace.

venues.name: 99 Sushi Bar & Restaurant
venues.note: Precise, classical sushi that has quietly held its star.

venues.name: LPM Restaurant & Bar
venues.note: Riviera cooking and a room that never goes out of fashion.

venues.name: Marmellata Bakery
venues.note: A waterfront pizzeria and bakery that became the city's happiest table.

venues.name: Niri Restaurant and Bar
venues.note: Beachfront Japanese with real polish, and a business lunch worth crossing town for.

venues.name: Mika
venues.note: A warm, generous kitchen at the water's edge, a Bib for the bill and the cooking both.

venues.name: Ryba
venues.note: Emirati seafood at the working harbour, Michelin's Opening of the Year.

venues.name: t'azal
venues.note: Levantine cooking done with heart, kept honest by the Bib inspectors.

venues.name: Al Mrzab
venues.note: Gulf and Emirati home cooking with a devoted local following.

venues.name: Beirut Sur Mer
venues.note: Beachfront Lebanese, bright, generous and full every night.

venues.name: Otoro
venues.note: Japanese comfort food at the waterfront, credentialed and easy to love.

venues.name: Almayass
venues.note: Armenian-Lebanese cooking with real character, a Bib regular.

venues.name: Zuma Abu Dhabi
venues.note: The izakaya template that set the tone for the region, still full every night.

venues.name: Coya Abu Dhabi
venues.note: Vivid Peruvian cooking and a room built for a good night out.

venues.name: Punjab Grill
venues.note: Refined North Indian dining with a Grand Canal view of the great mosque.

venues.name: Moksh
venues.note: Contemporary Indian by the Corniche, considered and well-kept.

venues.name: Namak
venues.note: Playful, modern Indian from a well-loved kitchen.

venues.name: Cafe Milano
venues.note: Polished Italian in the Four Seasons, dependable and quietly grand.

venues.name: Butcher & Still
venues.note: A 1920s-Chicago chophouse, serious steak and a serious bar.

venues.name: Dai Pai Dong
venues.note: Cantonese comfort cooking with genuine soul, on Al Maryah Island.

venues.name: Em Sherif Sea Café
venues.note: Seafront Lebanese from the Em Sherif name, generous and glamorous.

venues.name: Cipriani
venues.note: The Venetian classic, Bellinis, carpaccio and a room that knows its worth.

venues.name: Fouquet's
venues.note: Parisian brasserie dining beneath the Louvre's dome.

venues.name: Bord Eau by Nicolas Isnard
venues.note: Classic French cooking by a Burgundy chef, beside the Grand Canal.

venues.name: Villa Toscana
venues.note: Warm Tuscan cooking in a handsome St. Regis room.

venues.name: Mazi
venues.note: Modern Greek by the beach, bright, sunlit and generous.

venues.name: Tean
venues.note: Levantine cooking with a sea view on the cultural island.

venues.name: Mate
venues.note: Nikkei cooking, Japanese precision with a Latin pulse, by the beach.

venues.name: Li Beirut
venues.note: Elevated Lebanese with a Corniche view, glamorous and assured.

venues.name: Ray's Grill
venues.note: A steak-and-view room on the 62nd floor, the city laid out below.

venues.name: Finz
venues.note: An over-water seafood house that has quietly kept its following for years.

venues.name: Fishmarket
venues.note: Pick your catch from the ice and have it cooked to order, by the marina.

venues.name: Shang Palace
venues.note: Refined Chinese cooking in a serene canal-side room.

venues.name: Hoi An
venues.note: Vietnamese cooking in a lantern-lit room, gentle and quietly excellent.

venues.name: Silk & Spice
venues.note: Thai cooking with real fragrance and fire, a long-standing local favourite.

venues.name: Meylas
venues.note: Homestyle Emirati cooking from a young local kitchen, warm and honest.

venues.name: Yadoo's House
venues.note: Emirati family recipes served like a home lunch, the real thing.

venues.name: Kopitiam by Chandy's
venues.note: Singaporean-Malaysian coffee-shop cooking, done with real affection.

venues.name: Oii
venues.note: Playful pan-Asian plates at the waterfront, easy, modern and fun.

venues.name: Terra
venues.note: A plant-forward kitchen doing bright, vegetable-led cooking with intent.

venues.name: Louvre Abu Dhabi
venues.note: The Arab world's first universal museum, Jean Nouvel's floating dome, and its rain of light, are reason enough to come.
credentials: First universal museum in the Arab world

venues.name: Sheikh Zayed Grand Mosque
venues.note: The white marble heart of the capital, 82 domes, a courtyard of inlaid flowers, and the world's largest hand-knotted carpet within.
credentials: World's largest hand-knotted carpet, 5,627 sqm, over 2.2 billion knots

venues.name: Qasr Al Watan
venues.note: The working Presidential Palace, opened to the public, a domed hall of gold and mosaic, and a library of 50,000 titles under it.

venues.name: teamLab Phenomena Abu Dhabi
venues.note: A building made only for teamLab, 17,000 square metres of light, water and air that become the artwork. The children will not forget it.
credentials: World's largest digital-art museum, opened April 2025

venues.name: The Empty Quarter, Qasr Al Sarab
venues.note: The largest continuous sand desert on earth, met from a fortress of dunes, dawn walks, falconry, and a silence you feel.

venues.name: Guggenheim Abu Dhabi
venues.note: Frank Gehry's largest Guggenheim of all, the anchor of the cultural district, arriving on Saadiyat.

venues.name: Yas Marina Circuit
venues.note: Home of the season-closing Abu Dhabi Grand Prix, Formula 1's first day-to-night race, run under the arch of the Yas hotel's shifting light.
credentials: Host of the Formula 1 Abu Dhabi Grand Prix

venues.name: Ferrari World Abu Dhabi
venues.note: The world's first Ferrari-branded park, under its vast red roof, and Formula Rossa, still one of the fastest launch coasters ever built.
credentials: Guinness World Record, fastest rollercoaster launch (Formula Rossa)

venues.name: SeaWorld Yas Island
venues.note: A new-generation marine park with no orcas, eight ocean realms and a research centre, built around one of the world's largest aquariums.

venues.name: Jubail Mangrove Park
venues.note: The green lung of the coast, a boardwalk and kayak trails threading a protected mangrove forest, with flamingos and herons at the water's edge.

venues.name: Abu Dhabi Corniche
venues.note: Eight kilometres of manicured waterfront, the capital's promenade, with a Blue Flag beach and the skyline laid out across the Gulf.

venues.name: Saadiyat Island beaches & turtle nesting
venues.note: A protected white-sand coast where hawksbill turtles still nest, the calm, wild edge of the cultural island.

venues.name: Qasr Al Hosn
venues.note: The oldest stone building in the city, the 1761 watchtower and fort where Abu Dhabi began, now a museum of its own story.

venues.name: Warner Bros. World Abu Dhabi
venues.note: A fully indoor, fully air-conditioned world of Gotham and Cartoon Junction, a summer-proof day for families.
credentials: Among the world's largest indoor theme parks

venues.name: Yas Waterworld
venues.note: An Emirati-themed water park built around a pearl-diving legend, record-holding rides and gentler pools side by side.

venues.name: Mangrove & city helicopter tour
venues.note: The whole capital from the air, the great mosque, the islands and the mangrove maze in a single sweep.

venues.name: Ray's Bar
venues.note: The capital's highest bar, Level 62, the whole city and Gulf laid out below, cocktails to match the view.
credentials: The highest bar in Abu Dhabi (Level 62, Etihad Towers)

venues.name: Azura Panoramic Lounge
venues.area: The St. Regis Abu Dhabi, Corniche
venues.note: Three open-air terraces on the St. Regis roof, Mediterranean plates, jazz, and an uninterrupted sweep of the Corniche.
credentials: Rooftop of a Forbes Travel Guide 5-Star hotel

venues.name: CATCH Rooftop
venues.area: The St. Regis Abu Dhabi, Corniche
venues.note: A polished seafood room below, a late, lively rooftop above, a favourite last stop of a big night on the Corniche.
credentials: At The St. Regis Abu Dhabi, Forbes Travel Guide 5-Star

venues.name: Siddharta Lounge by Buddha-Bar
venues.note: The only rooftop over Yas Bay, the Buddha-Bar signature of low light, deep house and Asian-Mediterranean plates.
credentials: The only rooftop lounge over Yas Bay Waterfront

venues.name: Zuma Abu Dhabi
venues.note: The izakaya template for the region, and its bar is among the city's finest, a crowd, a resident DJ, and drinks done properly.

venues.name: Glo at Rosewood Abu Dhabi
venues.note: A day-to-night poolside lounge on the financial island, sculptural, easy, and quietly Rosewood-run.
credentials: At Rosewood Abu Dhabi, Condé Nast Traveler Readers' Choice top-10 Middle East hotel

venues.name: AT.35
venues.note: A refined lounge and bar high in the Etihad Towers, a considered list and a considered crowd, above the Corniche.
credentials: At the Conrad Abu Dhabi Etihad Towers, Forbes Travel Guide 5-Star

venues.name: MAD on Yas Island
venues.note: The biggest indoor club in the country, 360-degree projection, a serious sound system, and the graffiti wall out front.
credentials: The largest indoor club in the UAE
By the ADD-MIND group (WHITE Dubai, IRIS)
